info.name: Administrator API - Digital Examination Attendance System
info.description:
Import this collection into Postman to use every endpoint currently available to a staff member with the `ADMINISTRATOR` authority.

## Quick start
1. Import this collection and `Administrator.local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the environment.
3. Run **Login as Administrator**. It saves `accessToken` and `refreshToken` automatically.
4. Run the remaining requests; exam IDs are saved when possible.

## Authorization
All protected requests send `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`. The application uses exact Spring Security authorities; `ADMINISTRATOR` is **not** a role hierarchy. Therefore invigilator-only operations (check-in, QR lookup, incident creation, session start/end, and report generation) are not administrator endpoints unless the account is also assigned the `INVIGILATOR` role.

## Response convention
Most JSON endpoints return `{ success, message, data }`. Validation and domain errors use the same envelope with `success: false`; common statuses are 400 (invalid request), 401 (missing/invalid token), 403 (insufficient authority), and 409 (conflicting state). The list reports endpoint returns persisted report entity fields; depending on the persistence configuration, related-object fields may be serialized as nested objects or identifiers.

## Included administrator capabilities
- Create pending staff accounts and obtain their activation tokens
- View the administrator dashboard
- List examinations, registered students, and assigned venues
- View an examination's venue-allocation statistics
- View its attendance register and summary
- View every incident
- View generated reports

The current backend does not expose administrator CRUD endpoints for students, exams, venues, allocations, or roles, nor staff-list, update, or delete endpoints.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Authentication is public, but these requests are configured for the seeded administrator account.

request.description: Authenticates a staff account and returns `data.accessToken` and `data.refreshToken`. This request saves both values to the selected environment. Access tokens expire after five minutes in the default configuration.
Rotates a valid refresh token and returns a new access/refresh-token pair. The submitted refresh token is revoked after use; use the newly saved value next time.

Requires `ADMINISTRATOR`. Returns a system-wide overview: `todaysExaminations`, `todaysExaminationDetails`, present/absent counts, attendance percentage, total and today's incidents, venue occupancy, and generated-report count. Venue occupancy rows contain exam/venue identity, capacity, allocated students, checked-in students, and `occupancyPercentage`.

item.name: 3. Staff management
item.description: Administrator-only staff onboarding. The response includes an activation token, which is shown only once; deliver it through an appropriate secure channel.

request.description: Requires `ADMINISTRATOR`. Creates a staff account with status `PENDING` and no password, then returns the new staff details plus a one-time `activationToken` and its `expiresAt` timestamp. All fields are required; `email` must be unique and valid, and `role` must match a role already stored in the database (for example `LECTURER` or `INVIGILATOR`). Save and securely deliver the activation token: it is not retrievable through another endpoint.

item.name: 4. Examination oversight
item.description: Use **List Examinations** first. Its test script stores the first returned ID as `examSessionId`; replace the variable with the desired session before subsequent requests.

request.description: Requires `ADMINISTRATOR` or `LECTURER`. Lists all examination sessions. Each item includes `examSessionId`, course code, date and times, academic year, semester, exam type, and status.

item.name: List Registered Students for an Examination

request.description: Requires `ADMINISTRATOR` or `LECTURER`. Lists students registered for the selected examination. Items provide computer number, name, programme, year of study, photo path, and registration status. Use an existing `examSessionId`; an unknown ID produces a 400 response.
Requires `ADMINISTRATOR`, `LECTURER`, or `INVIGILATOR`. Lists the venues attached to the selected examination: `venueId`, `venueName`, `building`, and `capacity`.

Requires `ADMINISTRATOR` or `LECTURER`. Returns allocation statistics for one examination: registered/allocated totals, total venue capacity, `venueFills`, and the detailed `allocations` list (student, venue, and seat number). Administrator access is read-only: automatic allocation is lecturer-only.

Requires `ADMINISTRATOR`, `LECTURER`, or `INVIGILATOR`. Returns attendance records for the examination. Each record includes student and venue details, checker identity, check-in time, verification method, attendance status, script-submission flag, and any alert message.

Requires `ADMINISTRATOR`, `LECTURER`, or `INVIGILATOR`. Returns concise totals: `checkedIn`, `absent`, `scriptsCollected`, and `incidents`. This is read-only for administrators; recording attendance and scripts is invigilator-only.

Requires `ADMINISTRATOR` or `INVIGILATOR`. An administrator receives all incidents system-wide; an invigilator receives only their own reports. Items include examination and venue IDs, optional student details, incident type, description, severity, evidence path, reporter, and occurrence time. Creating incidents is invigilator-only.

Requires `ADMINISTRATOR`. Lists every persisted generated report. A report stores its ID, related exam session and generating staff references, title, report type, file path, generation timestamp, and summary. Administrators can view this index, but generation is invigilator-only and PDF download is lecturer-only in the current API.
